description: Replace the serial per-matrix torch.linalg.eigh (cuSOLVER syevd loop, 148 SMs idle one matrix at a time) with a genuinely batched symmetric eigensolver: a load_inline C++ extension calling cuSOLVER cusolverDnXsyevBatched (CUDA-13 batched syevd, no longer n<=32 capped) in one call over the whole batch, JOBZ vectors, dtype FP32. Benchmark the batched entry point on the n=512 b640 shape FIRST: if it internally serializes or rejects n>=512, pivot to multi-stream/grouped syevd overlapping the batch across CUDA streams. Emit L ascending and Q columns permuted to match.

Build a tensor-core batched Jacobi eigensolver that routes the O(n^3) interior onto B200 tensor cores the baseline never touches (it is 100% CUDA-core GEMV+sytrd). Use the symmetric two-sided/block-Jacobi formulation on A (orthogonal similarity J^T A J), or one-sided on A with explicit sign recovery, applying rotations as batched GEMM via torch.bmm (BF16/TF32) and/or Triton tl.dot; iterate to a HOST-VISIBLE off-diagonal-norm tolerance (not a fixed sweep count) so clustered/repeated/mixed benchmark cases still converge. Finish with an FP32 orthonormalization (CholeskyQR2 or Newton-Schulz) of Q and FP32 Rayleigh-quotient L=diag(Q^T A Q), sorted ascending with Q permuted to match.

Attack the profiled tridiagonalization bottleneck (baseline sytrd4_cta 22% + gemvx/symv/gemv2 matrix-VECTOR panel updates ~42%, all BLAS-2 CUDA-core, zero tensor-core). Build a batched two-step band reduction: full->banded via BLAS-3 blocked Householder using batched GEMM/syr2k on B200 tensor cores (BF16/TF32 panels, torch.bmm or a Triton kernel), then a cheap banded->tridiagonal + tridiagonal eigensolve (per-matrix QL/divide-and-conquer or torch path) on the narrow band. Emit FP32 Q (reorthonormalized via Newton-Schulz/CholeskyQR if low precision) and L via FP32 Rayleigh quotient, sorted ascending with Q permuted to match.

Pure-syevd is exhausted at 1.10x (its FP32 BLAS-2 tridiagonalization can't tensor-core). Open the GEMM-purest frontier path: a batched spectral divide-and-conquer eigensolver via the matrix sign function / polar decomposition. Split each matrix's spectrum with a Newton-Schulz (or QDWH) polar/sign iteration computed as batched BF16/TF32 torch.bmm (input_precision tf32x3 where accuracy needs it), forming the spectral projector P=(I+sign(A-sigma I))/2; recurse into the two invariant subspaces (deflate via QtAQ). CRITICAL: the polar factor only SPLITS the spectrum, it is NOT the eigenbasis - you must recurse and DIAGONALIZE the small base blocks (reuse the inherited batched cusolverDnXsyevBatched as the base-case solver), then reassemble Q. Jitter the split shift to avoid clustered/repeated eigenvalues landing on the contour (the clustered/rankdef/mixed benchmark cases). Emit Q FP32-orthonormalized (Newton-Schulz/CholeskyQR2) and L via FP32 Rayleigh quotient diag(QtAQ), sorted ascending with Q permuted to match.

Jacobi is ruled out (10.5x slower). Branch off the batched-syevd best 2332f1a0 (keep its 1.10x) and STACK a size/structure dispatcher that captures wins batched-syevd leaves on the table - additive, no new O(n^3) tensor-core solver (W0/W2 own that). Two mechanisms: (1) genuine rank-deficiency fast path for the rankdef/nearrank benchmark cases - the matrices have numerical rank 3n/4, so compute only the significant invariant subspace (e.g. a few subspace-iteration/randomized-range-finder steps on tensor cores, or a rank-revealing reduction) and complete the null space with a cheap orthonormal basis, instead of a full dense syevd; (2) squeeze the launch-bound small shapes (n=32/176/352 = 3/13 of the geomean). Dispatch on GENUINE numerical structure that passes all 39 test-shape residual gates - NOT benchmark seed/shape sniffing. Emit FP32 (Q,L), L ascending, Q permuted to match, orthonormality via FP32 CholeskyQR2/Newton-Schulz.

Band-reduction is ruled out; the data says the ONLY family that breaks the cuSOLVER-eigh ceiling is a GEMM-only solver. Take the frontier via QDWH-eig - the polar-decomposition spectral divide-and-conquer, mechanistically DISTINCT from worker-0's Newton-Schulz sign-function line: compute the polar factor of A-sigma I with the QR-based Dynamically Weighted Halley iteration (stacked [A;I] QR for ill-conditioned early steps, switching to the cheaper Cholesky-based form once well-conditioned), globally cubically convergent in <=6 iterations, all batched QR/Cholesky/GEMM on B200 tensor cores (TF32/BF16, tf32x3 where accuracy needs it). The QDWH polar factor gives the spectral projector P=(I+U_polar)/2 that SPLITS the spectrum at sigma - it is NOT the eigenbasis; recurse into the two invariant subspaces (deflate via QtAQ) until base blocks are small, then diagonalize base blocks with torch.linalg.eigh, and reassemble Q. QR/Cholesky-based QDWH is backward-stable and handles eigenvalues near the split more robustly than sign-squaring - but still jitter sigma off clustered/repeated eigenvalue locations (clustered/rankdef/mixed cases). Reuse your verified tail: FP32 Newton-Schulz/CholeskyQR2 reortho of Q, FP32 Rayleigh-quotient L=diag(QtAQ), power-of-two prescale, L ascending with Q permuted to match.

Complete the band-reduction pipeline you proved stage-1 of. Your tensor-core blocked-Householder full->band reduction (commit cfd7423e1) is fast and passes 39/39 - the ONLY missing piece you identified was a structure-aware stage 2 (torch.linalg.eigh ignores band/tridiagonal structure, saving ~0). Build that missing piece as a CUSTOM leaderboard-portable kernel (Triton or CUDA C++, stock CUDA only - no MAGMA/external libs, the remote build lacks them): a batched band->tridiagonal bulge-chase, then a custom batched TRIDIAGONAL eigensolver (implicit-shift QL/QR or tridiagonal divide-and-conquer) that exploits the O(n^2) tridiagonal structure instead of paying for a dense O(n^3) eigh. This is the published 4.1x-end-to-end approach (tensor-core reduction + structured tridiagonal solve). Keep the O(n^3) work on tensor cores (stage 1, already done) and make stage 2 cheap. Reuse your verified tail: FP32 Newton-Schulz/CholeskyQR2 reortho of the accumulated Q, FP32 Rayleigh-quotient L, power-of-two prescale, L ascending with Q permuted to match. Profile to confirm where time goes after stage 2 is structure-aware.

Your dead-end findings localized the entire remaining geomean to the dense n=512/1024 GEMV-bound sytrd interior, and named the one lever cuSOLVER's batched API cannot express: a reduced-precision two-stage solve with FP32 refinement. Build exactly that, branched off baseline. Stage A: get APPROXIMATE eigenpairs cheaply on tensor cores - a low-precision (BF16/TF32) tridiagonalization or a coarse approximate diagonalization, fast and sloppy. Stage B: REFINE to pass the gates entirely with batched GEMM (tensor-core), exploiting the loose ~1-2 digit tolerance - e.g. Rayleigh-Ritz: form the small projected matrix M=Q^T A Q (batched bmm), diagonalize the SMALL M, update Q<-Q@eigvecs(M); and/or a couple of subspace-iteration / Newton refinement steps. The point: replace cuSOLVER's expensive FP32 BLAS-2 sytrd with cheap tensor-core GEMM passes that the loose tolerance makes sufficient. Finish with FP32 CholeskyQR2/Newton-Schulz reortho of Q and FP32 Rayleigh-quotient L=diag(Q^T A Q), L ascending with Q permuted to match. Dispatch only on genuine numerical structure that passes all 39 test gates, never on benchmark seed/shape.

Every dead end so far shared one flaw: it delegated diagonalization to cuSOLVER (per-matrix launch serialization + FP32 BLAS-2 sytrd) or round-tripped through HBM via torch.bmm between library calls. The untried frontier architecture is a SINGLE FUSED custom CUDA C++ kernel, ONE CTA per matrix, the whole matrix RESIDENT IN SHARED MEMORY (n<=512 FP32 = 1MB > 228KB, so tile to a panel or use BF16/half SMEM storage; n=512 the dominant group), doing the entire eigensolve in-kernel - no cuSOLVER, no HBM round-trips between steps. This is the RIKEN EigenG-Batched / register-resident batched-eigensolver design (warp-per-matrix cooperative reduction): in-SMEM Householder tridiagonalization with warp-shuffle reductions + in-SMEM implicit-shift QL/divide-and-conquer, accumulating Q. Compile sm_100a. The key lever your own profiling found: keep everything in one precision in-kernel (BF16/half storage, FP32 accumulate) - the 51%-in-conversion tax dies when there is no per-op convert. Worker-1 saw a NAIVE unfused in-SMEM Jacobi at 333ms/round; the win is fusion + warp-cooperative reduction + no per-matrix kernel launch, not the rotation math. Emit FP32 (Q,L), FP32 reortho + Rayleigh L, L ascending with Q permuted to match. Profile iteration 1 with ncu to find the in-kernel bottleneck (occupancy/SMEM/registers).

Your reduced-precision idea was right but Stage-A block-Jacobi reintroduced the O(sweeps·n^3) wall. Pivot to the UNDEREXPLORED large-n / low-batch tail: the n=1024 b60 (4 shapes) and n=2048 b8 (1 shape) groups, where batched-syevd gives near-zero benefit (batch too small to fill 148 SMs) and where W0 (fused SMEM, n<=512 focus) and W2 (band reduction) are weakest. Branch off the syevd best 2332f1a0 and STACK a size-dispatched custom large-n path. Key: replace cuSOLVER's BLAS-2 GEMV sytrd with NON-ITERATIVE tensor-core BLAS-3. Try a custom blocked two-stage: TF32/BF16 tensor-core panel-blocked Householder (full->band) reduction done as batched GEMM/syr2k (NO per-sweep iteration), then for the narrow band either a custom tridiagonal QL or - since batch is tiny - overlap the per-matrix tridiagonal solves. Exploit the loose tolerance: the reduction can be low-precision with an FP32 Rayleigh-Ritz/Newton cleanup. Dispatch on matrix SIZE (n>=1024), not benchmark seed. Emit FP32 (Q,L), FP32 reortho + Rayleigh L, L ascending with Q permuted to match. Profile to confirm the large-n bottleneck moved off BLAS-2.

You ISOLATED the run's linchpin: your full->band reduction is ~1.6x faster than cuSOLVER (idealized ~30x), and the ONLY wall is the band/tridiagonal solve (cuSOLVER exploits no bandedness, no batched tridiagonal eigensolver in its API). Now BUILD that missing primitive yourself, completing your large-n pipeline. Branch off your own 59f2aaec (keeps the fast reduction; just replace the cuSOLVER band-solve). Build a CUSTOM batched TRIDIAGONAL eigensolver via PARALLEL BISECTION + INVERSE ITERATION (stock CUDA/Triton): eigenvalues by bisection on the Sturm-sequence sign-count (embarrassingly parallel across eigenvalues AND batch; the loose ~1-2 digit tolerance means few bisection steps), eigenvectors by inverse iteration solving (T-lambda I)x=b (O(n) per vector on a tridiagonal). This is mechanistically DISTINCT from worker-2, who is building a bulge-chase/QL tridiagonal solver - two different algorithms for the same critical primitive is deliberate. Watch the clustered/repeated/nearrank cases (inverse iteration needs reorthogonalization within eigenvalue clusters - the loose gate + your FP32 CholeskyQR2/Newton-Schulz reortho tail should absorb it; reorthogonalize within clusters). First reduce band->tridiagonal (bandwidth 1) if your reduction stops at a wider band. Emit FP32 (Q,L), L ascending with Q permuted to match. Profile to confirm the band-solve wall is gone.

Your SMEM wall was specific to the DENSE matrix (n<=168 fits) - but a TRIDIAGONAL matrix is only 2n floats (3KB at n=512), so it trivially fits in SMEM and your fused-kernel + ncu skills now apply where the wall does NOT bite. The run's linchpin is a custom batched tridiagonal eigensolver (W1 proved the tensor-core tridiagonalization is FREE; cuSOLVER has none). Branch off cfd7423e (worker-2's VERIFIED reduction: it already produces a tridiagonal T and just calls torch.linalg.eigh(T) on it - replace ONLY that slow per-matrix call). Build a custom batched tridiagonal eigensolver via DIVIDE-AND-CONQUER (Cuppen): recursively split T into two halves + rank-1 correction, solve the secular equation 1+rho*sum(z_i^2/(d_i-lambda))=0 for the merged eigenvalues (parallel root-finding, loose tolerance = few iterations), get merged eigenvectors from the secular roots (GEMM-friendly via the Lowner/eigenvector formula), back up the recursion. This is mechanistically DISTINCT from worker-1 (bisection+inverse-iteration) and worker-2 (bulge-chase/QL) - three different algorithms for the one critical primitive is deliberate. The dominant n=512 group has batch 640 = ample CTAs (no occupancy starvation, unlike your dense fused kernel). Watch deflation for clustered/repeated eigenvalues (equal d_i or zero z_i - standard D&C deflation). Emit FP32 (Q,L) back-transformed through the reduction's Q1, L ascending with Q permuted to match. ncu-profile the merge kernel.

Emit FP32 (Q,L) back-transformed through the reduction's accumulated Q1, L ascending with Q permuted to match. Profile to confirm the flood is gone and the reduction no longer dominates.

You pinpointed the run's ONE universal missing kernel: a custom batched band->tridiagonal BULGE-CHASE. Build exactly that, in situ, to close your own end-to-end large-n pipeline. Branch off your own 100c57b5 (already has your FAST full->band(64) GEMM reduction + your VALIDATED bisection+inverse-iteration tridiagonal solver - only the band->tridiagonal step in the middle is the slow PyTorch per-matrix QR that OOMs). The band is narrow (b=64 then recurse, or go straight to tridiagonal) so the working set is small and SMEM-resident - your bulge-chase does NOT hit worker-0's dense-SMEM wall. This assembles your three proven-fast pieces into the n=1024/2048 tail win (5/13 of geomean, ~70% BLAS-2 in the parent).
